changes.after: Handle a known failure with a message that explains what needs fixing.

before: toInt throws NumberFormatException when text is not a valid Int representation. Catch only the failure you intend to handle. A stack trace identifies an exception type and call frames; line numbers change as source changes.

This example reports a stable setting name rather than dumping arbitrary text. A successful parse skips the catch. If an error cannot be handled here, propagate it instead of silently substituting a misleading success value.
Expected output or behavior: minutes must be a whole number. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Remove the catch locally and identify the relevant application frame without depending on a fixed line number. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Debugging means finding why a program behaves incorrectly. Here, String.toInt throws NumberFormatException when text cannot be read as an Int. The catch handles that specific failure.

A useful error message names the value that needs attention. This message names minutes and explains the whole-number rule. It does not dump the original input or pretend the failed conversion succeeded.
The screen shows `minutes must be a whole number`. The text many cannot be read as an Int, so the matching catch runs.

A stack trace lists the error and the chain of function calls that led to it. Use it to find the relevant code, remembering that line numbers can change after edits. If this part of the program cannot handle an error, let the caller handle it instead of hiding it.
